HARPER LEE · 1960 · FICTION

To Kill a Mockingbird

In a small Alabama town during the 1930s, Scout Finch grows up alongside her brother Jem. Their father, lawyer Atticus Finch, defends a Black man wrongly accused of assaulting a white woman. Through Scout’s eyes, the novel examines racial injustice, courage, and the distance between appearances and reality.
